description: Table 1 is a single-panel data table (no sub-figures) titled "Calculated parameters (a, b, c), calculated cohesive energy (E_coh) and formation enthalpy (ΔH_f) of Fe–Mn–Al alloys". It has four columns: "Species", "a = b=c/nm", "E_coh/(eV·atom⁻¹)" and "ΔH_f/(eV·atom⁻¹)", and twelve rows listing Fe, FeAl, nine Fe1−xMnxAl compositions, MnAl, Mn and Al. Printed values are: Fe 0.275 / −8.981 / 0; FeAl 0.570 / −6.947 / −0.391; Fe0.875Mn0.125Al 0.572 / −6.920 / −0.376; Fe0.75Mn0.25Al 0.574 / −6.889 / −0.357; Fe0.625Mn0.375Al 0.576 / −6.868 / −0.347; Fe0.5Mn0.5Al 0.578 / −6.843 / −0.334; Fe0.375Mn0.625Al 0.580 / −6.824 / −0.328; Fe0.25Mn0.75Al 0.581 / −6.794 / −0.309; Fe0.125Mn0.875Al 0.582 / −6.744 / −0.269; MnAl 0.584 / −6.568 / −0.215; Mn 0.354 / −9.313 / 0; Al 0.405 / −3.724 / 0. The table is thus a first-principles (DFT) results table: the cubic lattice parameter of the Fe1−xMnxAl series increases monotonically from 0.570 nm (FeAl) to 0.584 nm (MnAl) with rising Mn content, while cohesive energy increases (becomes less negative) from −6.947 to −6.568 eV·atom⁻¹ and formation enthalpy increases from −0.391 to −0.215 eV·atom⁻¹. All alloy E_coh and ΔH_f values are negative, which the text uses to argue thermodynamic stability, with FeAl identified as the most stable composition.

observations.observation: Table 1 lists four columns: Species, a = b=c/nm, E_coh/(eV·atom⁻¹) and ΔH_f/(eV·atom⁻¹).
The table contains 12 rows: Fe, FeAl, nine Fe1−xMnxAl compositions (x = 0.125 to 0.875), MnAl, Mn and Al.
The lattice parameter a = b = c increases monotonically across the Fe1−xMnxAl series from 0.570 nm for FeAl to 0.584 nm for MnAl.
Pure Fe, Mn and Al have printed lattice parameters of 0.275, 0.354 and 0.405 nm respectively.
Cohesive energy becomes less negative with increasing Mn content, from −6.947 eV·atom⁻¹ (FeAl) to −6.568 eV·atom⁻¹ (MnAl).
Formation enthalpy becomes less negative with increasing Mn content, from −0.391 eV·atom⁻¹ (FeAl) to −0.215 eV·atom⁻¹ (MnAl).
Formation enthalpy is printed as 0 for the pure elements Fe, Mn and Al.
The caption states the table reports calculated parameters (a, b, c), calculated cohesive energy (E_coh) and formation enthalpy (ΔH_f) of Fe–Mn–Al alloys.

The citing text states the cohesive energy of the Fe1−xMnxAl alloys varies from −6.568 to −6.947 eV·atom⁻¹ and the formation enthalpy from −0.215 to −0.391 eV·atom⁻¹, matching the printed table values.
The citing text states that all calculated formation enthalpy and cohesive energy values are negative, indicating the Fe1−xMnxAl alloys are thermally stable.

The citing text concludes that FeAl is the most stable alloy in the Fe1−xMnxAl system, because it has the lowest (most negative) formation enthalpy and the most negative cohesive energy among the alloys.
The citing text notes both cohesive energy and formation enthalpy increase with Mn content.
The citing text mentions that Figure 2 depicts the calculated cohesive energy and formation enthalpy for different Mn contents, i.e. this table's data are also plotted elsewhere in the paper.
